---
title: "Surveys"
page-layout: article
---

Surveys are book-length expository work: a sustained treatment of one area, built to teach it rather than to settle a single open question. Where a [paper](/papers/index.qmd) states and argues one precise result, a survey lays out a whole framework or subfield chapter by chapter — definitions, running examples, and worked constructions building on one another — so a reader can come in without the background and leave able to use the material.

Like papers, surveys here are generated (co-authored) with the help of AI, and the same honesty about that applies: a survey is only as good as the definitions and proofs it contains, and every chapter is open to the same scrutiny a paper's single result would get.

Each entry below links to the compiled PDF and its LaTeX source.
